The Agency still has that monopoly but it is now possible to bypass it with the imperative reasons set out in Article 52c. The most important is the introduction of a European directive that allows all members to make independent decisions on the ban on GMOs, so is Croatia's GMO free country. This legislative advantage of individual EU Member States over the European Government has been achieved by implementing the measures contained in Council Directive 412. This means if Croatia, for example. wants to keep the country's tourism image with traditional country fruits, it can activate the imperative reasons of the directive and ban the planting of GMO crops. This protection mechanism was not possible under the old law and GMOs have now become legal and recorded in Article 52c but the fundamental question is whether GMOs are more harmful or pesticide-treated crops? So the Hungarians didn't go great, and I didn't have a great time, but the Hungarians went even worse. Therefore, to return to the past, on the basis of the judgment of C-26/13 of the EU Court of Justice, it was ruled that the currency clause in Hungary, the currency clause CHF, was invaluable, and therefore Hungary passed a law which, among other things, converted these loans into forints. And after that, one consumer, i.e. the consumer, Mrs. However, Dunai sued the bank and asked for its contract to be declared worthless. On the basis of the complaint, the national Hungarian court asked the EU court to answer some previous questions. And the basic answer is whether the debtor, after converting the loan, is entitled to compensation. Is he actually entitled to a worthless contract? In short, as the EU court ruled by ruling C-18/17, he decided, firstly, that if the currency clause is zero, that in this case it is the main subject matter of the contract and that, in that case, if the main subject matter of the contract is zero, the EU court should also consider that the contract should be void. In other words, if we transfer this to the Franak case in Croatia, all the contracts with the CHF currency clause should, in the opinion of the EU court, be harmless. That's the first thing. It's another thing. What the EU court says is next. That the law should not reduce the consumer's right to compensation given to it by EU law. However, that it must be established whether that money which has been remunerated because of the application of unfair contractual provisions, and we of the Franak Association and myself have already proved by law that no amount has been paid back on the basis of unfair contractual provisions, and hence, the Supreme Court of the Republic of Croatia, when it will apply the judgment of the EU Court of Justice C-118/17 in the decision on the Franak case, for the converted loans, will have to apply the rule of the EU court which says that it must not reduce the consumer's right to compensation. Therefore, they will have to rule that we have the right to compensation despite having converted CHF loans. Next thing. The right of credit users, i.e. the consumer and his interest, are always ahead of the interest of the unfair bank. So, if it is found that the bank was unfair, then the consumer has the right to compensation and it must not be seen that the bank may be damaged, and I must say that the bank will not be damaged in Croatia, not one, the banks have had more than 30 billion kunas of liquidity and will only reduce liquidity if they return what they unfairly acquired. And finally, another important thing is that the consumer has the right to choose whether to remain in a contract that is worthless, unfair or under the law, or to demand that the contract be declared null. So he has a right to stay in that contract, if he wants to, if that's better for him. That's what the EU court says. The next thing that is also important is that the Supreme Court of the Republic of Croatia, on the basis of this judgment, has the right to even the case law, but despite the fact that it is now equating judicial practice and that it will even the caselaw, lower courts still have the right to ask the previous questions of the EU court regardless of the decision of the Supreme Court of Justice of the Republic of Croatia.
